nodes.summary: The supremum, in $[0, \infty]$, of the Lebesgue areas of all ambidextrous sofas is at most the supremum of the Lebesgue areas of all sofas. This holds because every ambidextrous sofa is a sofa.
nodes.title: The ambidextrous optimal area is at most the optimal area

nodes.summary: The ambidextrous optimal area is the supremum, taken in $[0, \infty]$, of the Lebesgue areas of all ambidextrous sofas $K \subseteq \mathbb{C}$.
nodes.title: Optimal area of ambidextrous sofas

nodes.summary: The supremum of the areas of ambidextrous sofas, taken in $[0, \infty]$, is at most $22195/10000 = 2.2195$.

nodes.summary: A set $K \subseteq \mathbb{C}$ can pass the Z corridor if there is a real number $D$ such that, for every real $d \ge D$, $K$ can pass the Z corridor with corner separation $d$; that is, $K$ passes whenever the corners are sufficiently separated.
nodes.title: Passing the Z corridor for all large separations

nodes.title: Passing the Z corridor at a given separation

nodes.summary: A set $K \subseteq \mathbb{C}$ can pass the corridor if there are continuous maps $u$ from $[0, 1]$ to the unit circle $\{w \in \mathbb{C} : |w| = 1\}$ and $c$ from $[0, 1]$ to $\mathbb{C}$ such that, writing $K_t = \{u(t) z + c(t) : z \in K\}$ for the position of $K$ at time $t$, $K_0$ lies in the entrance arm, $K_1$ lies in the exit arm, and $K_t$ lies in the corridor for every $t \in [0, 1]$.
nodes.title: Passing the corridor

nodes.summary: The mirrored corridor is the set of points $z \in \mathbb{C}$ with $\operatorname{Re} z \ge -1$ and $0 \le \operatorname{Im} z \le 1$ (the horizontal arm, extending to the right) together with the points $z$ with $-1 \le \operatorname{Re} z \le 0$ and $\operatorname{Im} z \ge 0$ (the vertical arm, extending upward). It is the reflection of the corridor in the imaginary axis, so passing it requires the opposite turn.
nodes.title: Mirrored corridor

nodes.summary: For a real number $d$, the Z-shaped corridor with corner separation $d$ is the set of points $z \in \mathbb{C}$ lying in at least one of three pieces: the lower horizontal arm, where $\operatorname{Re} z \le 1$ and $0 \le \operatorname{Im} z \le 1$; the middle channel, where $0 \le \operatorname{Re} z \le 1$ and $0 \le \operatorname{Im} z \le 2 + d$; and the upper horizontal arm, where $\operatorname{Re} z \ge 0$…
nodes.title: Z-shaped corridor

nodes.summary: The corridor is the L-shaped set of points $z \in \mathbb{C}$ with $\operatorname{Re} z \le 1$ and $0 \le \operatorname{Im} z \le 1$ (the horizontal arm, extending to the left) together with the points $z$ with $0 \le \operatorname{Re} z \le 1$ and $\operatorname{Im} z \ge 0$ (the vertical arm, extending upward): two perpendicular semi-infinite arms of width one.
nodes.title: Corridor

nodes.summary: The entrance arm of the mirrored corridor is the set of points $z \in \mathbb{C}$ with $\operatorname{Re} z \ge 0$ and $0 \le \operatorname{Im} z \le 1$: the part of its horizontal arm beyond the corner square $-1 \le \operatorname{Re} z \le 0$, $0 \le \operatorname{Im} z \le 1$.
nodes.title: Entrance arm of the mirrored corridor

nodes.summary: The entrance region of the Z corridor is the closed half-strip $\{z \in \mathbb{C} : \operatorname{Re} z \le 0,\ 0 \le \operatorname{Im} z \le 1\}$, the part of its horizontal entrance arm to the left of the middle channel.
nodes.title: Entrance arm of the Z corridor

nodes.summary: The entrance region of the unit right-angle corridor is the closed half-strip $\{z \in \mathbb{C} : \operatorname{Re} z \le 0,\ 0 \le \operatorname{Im} z \le 1\}$, the part of its horizontal arm to the left of the corner square.
nodes.title: Entrance of the corridor

nodes.summary: The exit region of the mirrored unit corridor is the closed half-strip $\{z \in \mathbb{C} : -1 \le \operatorname{Re} z \le 0,\ \operatorname{Im} z \ge 1\}$, the part of its vertical arm above its corner square.
nodes.title: Exit of the mirrored corridor

nodes.summary: For a real number $d$ (the corner separation), the exit region of the Z corridor with separation $d$ is the closed half-strip $\{z \in \mathbb{C} : \operatorname{Re} z \ge 1,\ 1 + d \le \operatorname{Im} z \le 2 + d\}$, the part of its horizontal exit arm to the right of the middle channel.
nodes.title: Exit arm of the Z corridor

nodes.summary: The exit region of the unit right-angle corridor is the closed half-strip $\{z \in \mathbb{C} : 0 \le \operatorname{Re} z \le 1,\ \operatorname{Im} z \ge 1\}$, the part of its vertical arm above the corner square.
nodes.title: Exit of the corridor

nodes.summary: The moving sofa constant, the supremum of the areas of connected Lebesgue-measurable planar shapes that a continuous rigid motion can carry through the right-angled corridor of width $1$, is at least $2.2195$.

nodes.summary: A set $K \subseteq \mathbb{C}$ is an ambidextrous sofa when it is a sofa and there is a real number $D$ such that, for every corner separation $d \ge D$, a single motion places $K$ inside the entrance arm of the Z corridor with separation $d$ at time $0$, inside its exit arm at time $1$, and inside that corridor at every time; such a passage turns once in each direction.
nodes.title: Ambidextrous sofa shapes

nodes.summary: A set $K \subseteq \mathbb{C}$ is a sofa when it is Lebesgue measurable, nonempty and connected, and can be moved through the unit right-angle corridor: there is a motion (a rotation by a unit complex number and a translation, both varying continuously with time $t \in [0, 1]$) that places $K$ inside the corridor's entrance region at time $0$, inside its exit region at time $1$, and inside the corridor at every…

nodes.summary: Let $m$ be a motion, $t \in [0, 1]$ a time, and write $m_t(z)$ for the position of a point $z \in \mathbb{C}$ under $m$ at time $t$. Then $|m_t(z) - m_t(w)| = |z - w|$ for all $z, w \in \mathbb{C}$.

nodes.summary: A motion consists of a continuous map $t \mapsto u_t$ from $[0, 1]$ to the unit circle $\{u \in \mathbb{C} : |u| = 1\}$ (the rotation) and a continuous map $t \mapsto c_t$ from $[0, 1]$ to $\mathbb{C}$ (the translation).

nodes.summary: The motion with no rotation that sends a point $z$ at time $t \in [0,1]$ to $z + \tau(t)$, where $\tau(t) = -2t$ for $t \le 1/2$ and $\tau(t) = -1 + (2t - 1)i$ for $t \ge 1/2$: it moves a shape one unit to the left during the first half of the time interval and then one unit upward.
nodes.title: The square's translation through the mirrored corner

nodes.summary: The square's translation through the Z corridor at separation $d = 1$: the motion with no rotation that sends a point $z$ at time $t \in [0,1]$ to $z + \tau(t)$, where $\tau(t) = 3t - 1$ for $t \le 1/3$, $\tau(t) = 2(3t - 1)i$ for $1/3 \le t \le 2/3$, and $\tau(t) = (3t - 2) + 2i$ for $t \ge 2/3$.
nodes.title: The square's translation through the Z corridor at separation one

nodes.summary: For a real number $d$, the motion with no rotation that sends a point $z$ at time $t \in [0,1]$ to $z + \tau(t)$, where $\tau(t) = 3t - 1$ for $t \le 1/3$, $\tau(t) = (1 + d)(3t - 1)i$ for $1/3 \le t \le 2/3$, and $\tau(t) = (3t - 2) + (1 + d)i$ for $t \ge 2/3$: it translates a shape by $1$, then by $(1 + d)i$, then by $1$, each segment taking a third of the time interval.

nodes.summary: The motion with no rotation that sends a point $z$ at time $t \in [0,1]$ to $z + \tau(t)$, where $\tau(t) = 2t - 1$ for $t \le 1/2$ and $\tau(t) = (2t - 1)i$ for $t \ge 1/2$: it moves a shape one unit to the right during the first half of the time interval and then one unit upward.

can_prove.label: ready to prove
can_prove.meaning: Statement is in Lean and nothing it needs is blocked, so the proof can start.

can_state.label: ready to state
can_state.meaning: Everything its statement uses is in Lean, so the statement can be written in Lean.

conditional.label: conditionally proved
conditional.meaning: Proof compiles, but rests on an open statement without a recorded Lean proof.

fully_proved.label: fully proved
fully_proved.meaning: Proved, and every prerequisite is fully proved too.

inventory_checked.label: inventory checked
inventory_checked.meaning: Module inventory checked in full; it records inspection, not a mathematical proof.

inventory_pending.label: inventory pending
inventory_pending.meaning: Module inventory not yet checked in full; it records inspection, not a mathematical proof.

not_ready.label: not ready
not_ready.meaning: Needs more blueprint work before it can be attempted.

proved.label: proved
proved.meaning: Proof compiles, but something it rests on is not finished.

stated.label: statement formalized
stated.meaning: Statement is in Lean; the proof is not.
